outline.notes: Direct answer in first 100 words (brief intro) and 4 one-sentence key takeaways above this H2. General coordination and booking on your behalf. Any statement on accreditation or consumer rights only as ACCC, ATAS, Smartraveller or Moneysmart state it [[VERIFY: wording and source]].

outline.h2: What you can book yourself, and where it gets harder

outline.notes: Affirm many couples book flights and stays themselves. Then questions, not claims: guest travel and rooms, many suppliers' dates and terms, payments in several currencies. No statistics, no scare framing. Gap: no top-10 result is honest about DIY.

outline.h2: Questions to ask before you hire an advisor
outline.answers: Brief must_include checklist; FAQ 'What should I ask before hiring a travel advisor?' and 'What is ATAS accreditation?'; NY PAA 'How does a travel advisor make money?' answered neutrally via 'Is the fee agreed in writing?'
outline.notes: Numbered checklist, applies to any advisor: accreditation scheme [[VERIFY: ATAS]]; fee in writing before work begins (brand-facts line allowed here); inclusions in writing; cancellation and change terms per booking; travel insurance, pointing to Smartraveller [[VERIFY]].
